question: What minimum vertical clearance is required for overhead signs over the pavement and shoulders?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Overhead signs must provide a vertical clearance of not less than 17 feet, measured to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge, over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders. Reduced clearances are permitted only where nearby structures have lesser vertical clearance (or in special cases such as tunnels), and certain preferential-lane signs on median barriers may be mounted higher so that at least 17 feet of clearance is maintained. Standards (mandatory): - "Overhead signs shall provide a vertical clearance of not less than 17 feet to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, except where the structure on which the overhead signs are to be mounted or other structures along the roadway near the sign structure have a lesser vertical clearance." (shown in [Image 2]) - "Signs that are post-mounted on a median barrier that overhang any portion of the traveled way shall be mounted with a vertical clearance that complies with that of overhead signs." (shown in [Image 2]) Options (permitted): - If the vertical clearance of other structures along the roadway near the sign structure is less than 16 feet, the vertical clearance to an overhead sign structure or support may be as low as 1 foot higher than the vertical clearance of the other structures in order to improve the visibility of the overhead signs (shown in [Image 2]). - Where lateral clearance is limited, Preferential Lane regulatory signs post-mounted on a median barrier that are 72 inches or less in width may be mounted higher, "such that the vertical clearance to the bottom of the sign, light fixture, or structural support, whichever is lowest, is not less than 17 feet above any portion of the pavement and shoulders." - Where lateral clearance is limited, warning signs applicable only to a preferential lane on a median barrier may likewise be mounted higher so that the vertical clearance "is not less than 17 feet above any portion of the pavement and shoulders." - The same 17-foot minimum applies where Preferential Lane guide signs 72 inches or less in width are mounted higher due to limited lateral clearance. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-2, panel H ("Overhead sign"), illustrates an overhead-mounted street name sign with a "17 ft MIN." vertical clearance dimension above the roadway and a 6-foot lateral offset for the support. - [Image 2] Contains the governing Standard text requiring 17 feet of vertical clearance for overhead signs over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, along with the Options for reduced clearance near lower structures. - [Image 3] Shows examples of overhead guide signs at an intersection (Figure 2D-10, Sheet 2), illustrating the type of overhead installations to which the clearance requirement applies. - [Image 4] Shows overhead Arrow-per-Lane and conventional guide signs at an intersection (Figure 2D-10, Sheet 1), further illustrating overhead sign installations. - [Image 5] Section 2E.19 (Overhead Sign Installations) notes that "Vertical clearance of overhead signs is discussed in Section 2A.15." Citations: - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Page 100 - Page 344 - Section 2G.03 Option §14 (p.411) - Section 2G.08 Option §4 (p.419) - Section 2G.10 Option §18 (p.422)
gold_answer: At least 17 feet, except where nearby structures or special constrained structures qualify for the specific exceptions in Section 2A.15.
